summary:
Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, offline-capable Mission Control simulator designed for learners ages 7–12 to experience real lunar engineering trade-offs at Shackleton Crater. Instead of simple right-or-wrong trivia, players act as Junior Flight Directors managing three coupled outpost subsystems—Solar Power (SYS-PWR), Life Support (SYS-ECLSS), and Radiation Shielding (SYS-RAD)—across five lunar sols where every choice carries a real resource cost.

Grounded in live and archived telemetry from NASA’s DONKI Space Weather API, the NASA Image and Video Library API, and NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), the simulator translates complex astrophysics into plain language through an interactive Space Glossary, hover-to-preview resource deltas, an animated lunar habitat cross-section, and an embedded AI Mission Copilot chatbot. Built as a Progressive Web App (PWA) with zero logins or downloads, it runs seamlessly online or 100% offline on any school Chromebook, tablet, or phone.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Astronaut Mission Trainer places young players (ages 7–12) in command of a lunar outpost at the Moon’s South Pole. Across five lunar sols, players face realistic operational crises—coronal mass ejections, electrostatic lunar regolith dust on solar arrays, hydroponic oxygen demand, high-gain Earth telemetry downlinks, and -130°C crater nightfall. Every decision involves genuine engineering trade-offs: boosting water-wall radiation shielding consumes battery reserves and hydroponic water, while maximizing grow lights drains power. Before locking in a command, players can hover or focus on decision cards to preview exact + and - resource changes and watch an interactive SVG lunar habitat visually respond in real time.

Educational & Accessibility Impact:

To eliminate jargon barriers for elementary and middle-school learners, we built:

  • Interactive AI Mission Copilot Chatbot: Allows students to ask natural-language space questions and receive plain-language explanations grounded in mission telemetry.
  • Tap-to-Decode Space Glossary: Explains terms like Solar Flare, Radiation Dose, Regolith, and Hydroponics in kid-friendly language.
  • Inclusive Design: Features an Easy-Read typography toggle, colorblind-safe icons paired with numeric telemetry bars, full keyboard/ARIA screen-reader support, and synthesized Quindar Mission Control audio.
  • 100% Offline PWA Architecture: Configured with a Service Worker (vite-plugin-pwa) and bundled local fallback datasets so classrooms and families can play with zero internet connection, zero accounts, and zero downloads.

Tools, Technologies & SI Disclosure:

Built with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Web Audio API, and vite-plugin-pwa. Super Intelligence (SI) tools were used to assist with code scaffolding, educational text drafting, and powering the in-app Copilot assistant, while all NASA telemetry, science facts, and mission datasets are explicitly cited and separated from SI-generated elements.
